payload.reason: The evidence provides insights into the criteria used by raters to evaluate classifier outputs, specifically focusing on the appropriateness of predicted error types.

claims.text: Raters selected 'Bad' when the predicted error type was not appropriate for the edit, often due to POS or parse errors.
Raters selected 'Good' or 'Acceptable' when they believed the predicted error types characterized the edits appropriately, despite potential noise from automatic edit extraction.
The evaluation was subjective, with raters focusing on the appropriateness of error types rather than the accuracy of edit boundaries.
